# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet, so I cannot safely cut anything. I need Mute to read the manual and relay its required wire position through Deaf. I will use a simple counting protocol: repeated 👍 gestures, one per wire position; Deaf should announce that count aloud so I can hear it next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual. Relay the required wire position to Deaf using that many repeated thumbs-up gestures: one thumbs-up means wire 1, two means wire 2, and so on. Ask Deaf to speak the counted number aloud in their turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb shows display 0 and a white light. Wires from left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Blind signalled thumbs-up.

The tactile view still reveals nothing about the wires, so I cannot act safely. Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, white light, and wire colours in positions 1–5. The manual is still the missing rule. I am asking Mute to convert the manual’s answer into a count of thumbs-up gestures for Deaf, who can then tell me the number aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Using the display 0, white light, and the wire colours Deaf reported, determine the required wire position from the manual. Gesture that position to Deaf as that many repeated thumbs-up symbols: 1 for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3, 4 for wire 4, or 5 for wire 5. Deaf should speak the number aloud next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled five thumbs-up gestures. The bomb still shows display 0, white light, and wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green.

Mute’s five thumbs-up gestures encode wire position 5. Deaf confirms the same bomb state and reports that count, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, yellow light. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut.

Wire 5 was correct. The new state is display 0 with a yellow light; the remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, and 4 white. I need the manual’s rule for this state before cutting again, so I am asking Mute to signal the resulting position to Deaf with the established count protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, with wire 5 already cut. Use the manual to determine the next wire. Signal Deaf with that many thumbs-up gestures: 1 through 4 for the corresponding wire position. Deaf should announce the count aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled three thumbs-up gestures. Current state remains display 0, yellow light; wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut.

Mute’s three thumbs-up gestures indicate wire position 3. The current state is unchanged, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, blue light. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 red, 5 cut.

Wire 3 was correct. The new state is display 0 with a blue light; remaining wires are 1 yellow, 2 white, and 4 red, with wires 3 and 5 cut. I need Mute’s manual-derived choice, so I will request the next wire using the established thumbs-up count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 red, 5 cut. Use the manual to determine the next wire. Signal Deaf with repeated thumbs-up gestures encoding its position: 1 for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3, 4 for wire 4, or 5 for wire 5. Deaf should announce the count aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled one thumbs-up gesture. Current state: display 0, blue light. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 red, 5 cut.

Mute’s one thumbs-up indicates wire position 1. The current state is display 0 with a blue light, and wires 3 and 5 are already cut. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, green light. Wires left to right: 1 cut, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut.

Wire 1 was correct. The new state is display 0 with a green light; the remaining wires are 2 red and 4 white, while 1, 3, and 5 are cut. I need the manual’s next choice, so I will request it from Mute using the established gesture-count protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 0, green light; wires 1 cut, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. Use the manual to determine the next wire. Signal Deaf with repeated thumbs-up gestures encoding its position: 1 for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3, 4 for wire 4, or 5 for wire 5. Deaf should announce the count aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled four thumbs-up gestures, likely indicating wire 4. Current state: display 0, green light. Wires: 1 cut, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut.

Mute’s four thumbs-up gestures indicate wire position 4. The current state is display 0 with a green light, and wire 4 is the indicated uncut wire, so I will cut it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
